title: A separated morphism unramified at the points of a fibre is etale locally a closed-immersion decomposition near them
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $s\in S$, and let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in X$ ($n\ge0$) be points with $f(x_i)=s$ such that $f$ is unramified at each $x_i$: every $x_i$ has an open neighbourhood $X_i\subseteq X$ such that $f|_{X_i}:X_i\to S$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then there are an etale morphism $g:U\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and a point $u\in U$ with $g(u)=s$, and a decomposition of the fibre product $X_U=X\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] into pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes $X_U=W\amalg\coprod_{i=1}^n\coprod_{j=1}^{m_i}V_{i,j}$ (integers $m_i\ge0$; $W$ and the $V_{i,j}$ open subschemes of $X_U$, pairwise disjoint, covering $X_U$), such that (1) for all $i,j$ the composite $V_{i,j}\hookrightarrow X_U\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2}U$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose image contains $u$; (2) no point of $W$ lying over $u\in U$ maps under $\mathrm{pr}_1:X_U\to X$ to any of $x_1,\ldots,x_n$. In particular, if $f^{-1}(\{s\})=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}$, then no point of $W$ lies over $u$.
